subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should explicit `skills.entries.<skill>.env` keys that match sensitive-name patterns be allowed into the active skill host-run exec environment, and what guard prevents those same skill secrets from reaching unrelated generic exec children?
rationale: The requested behavior matches current docs and user reports, but it deliberately moves credential-shaped values across a process/exec boundary that overlaps an open secret-leak issue.

options.title: Allow explicit skill env with leak guard
options.body: Keep the documented host-run skill env contract by allowing configured per-skill keys while preserving hard-blocked host vars and adding/keeping tests that unrelated generic exec children do not inherit skill secrets.

options.title: Require manifest-declared sensitive keys
options.body: Only allow credential-shaped keys when the skill declares them through metadata, which is stricter but would require updating bundled and external skills such as `gog`.

options.title: Reject credential-shaped skill env injection
options.body: Document that password/token-shaped skill env keys are intentionally blocked and require users to use another secret path, accepting the current GOG/headless VPS breakage.

recommendation.title: Allow explicit skill env with leak guard
recommendation.body: Keep the documented host-run skill env contract by allowing configured per-skill keys while preserving hard-blocked host vars and adding/keeping tests that unrelated generic exec children do not inherit skill secrets.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily a SecretRef/credential-to-exec security boundary, and joshavant has the strongest merged history on that surface.
